MNT is known to be helpful during pregnancy. However, to 
be most effective, dietitians and nutritionists must consider all 
current issues. A pregnant woman may have poor weight gain 
but also low iron levels; foods that address both issues should 
be used. She may have low calcium intake but also have GDM, 
thus modifying how she is counseled. She may have cultural 
practices that could affect her nutritional status (e.g., veiling 
and vitamin D). She may have preexisting medical conditions 
that must be managed, including carrying parasitic infections 
common in her home country. She may develop issues during 
pregnancy (e.g., anemia, gallstones, or GDM) but also may find 
medical issues that are not directly related to the pregnancy 
(e.g., cancer or a Crohn’s disease flare-up). She may experience 
trauma from a motor vehicle accident or physical abuse that
